top.title: Truro's En-Neyah 'sitting up and chatting' after collapse
top.description: Morrocan-born En-Neyah is a former Republic of Ireland youth international [Shutterstock] Truro City midfielder Yassine En-Neyah is in a stable condition after collapsing during the warm-up for his side's National League South game on Saturday. The game between Folkestone Invicta and Truro was abandoned before kick-off due to the incident. The 26-year-old was taken by ambulance to the William Harvey Hospital in Ashford for treatment. "He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation," a Truro City statement read. "The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City's medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club. "Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. "There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too." En-Neyah joined Truro from Irish side Waterford in February 2023, having previously been on the books at Nottingham Forest. Truro were second in the table before this afternoon's matches, with Folkestone in 15th place. An update on En-Neyah's condition, and any rearranged date for the fixture, will be announced in due course. Related internet links Truro City FC

top.title: Norris takes pole in rain-delayed qualifying
top.description: Lando Norris has won two races this season, in Hungary and the Netherlands [Reuters] McLaren's Lando Norris took pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in a wet qualifying session at Interlagos delayed by nearly an hour and a half for heavy rain. Norris beat fellow Briton George Russell by 0.204 seconds, and the Mercedes driver was fuming that he could have been faster had he not been told by his engineer to abort a faster lap. In any case, Russell has a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his permitted number of engine parts, promoting team-mate and new world champion Kimi Antonelli to second. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc qualified fourth but has a 10-place grid penalty which promotes Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson to third. The New Zealander was one of a number of drivers to have their best qualifying session of the year thanks to the levelling effect of the wet weather. Also among them were Audi's Nico Hulkenberg, who qualified sixth and will start fourth, Haas driver Oliver Bearman, who was eighth and will start sixth, and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso, who was ninth and will move up one place to eighth. top.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Lando Norris takes pole in soaking wet qualifying
top.description: Motorsport photo McLaren's Lando Norris has claimed pole in a wet qualifying session at Formula 1's Brazilian Grand Prix, beating George Russell on a treacherous Interlagos circuit. In a challenging session that was red-flagged by over an hour due to heavy rain and standing water, Norris topped the final Q3 shootout with a 1m27.470s lap on the intermediate tyres, pipping Mercedes' Russell by two tenths. Russell was nursing a five-place grid penalty for a power unit change, but was still incensed by his Mercedes team asking him to abort his second flying lap in Q3. Antonelli qualified third, six tenths behind Norris, with Charles Leclerc fourth in the Ferrari . As well as Russell's demotion, Leclerc's 10-place engine penalty elevated fifth-placed Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson to third on Sunday's grid. Lawson is under pressure to retain his seat as Racing Bulls considers promoting reserve driver Nikola Tsolov instead, but the New Zealander delivered a standout performance to give the squad food for thought. Nico Hulkenberg also shone in sixth for Audi , followed by Red Bull's Isack Hadjar and Haas driver Oliver Bearman . Fernando Alonso and Alex Albon completed the top 10 on Saturday. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes In Q2 Alonso was the first driver to switch to intermediates as he aimed to lift his Aston Martin out of the belly of the pack. Other soon followed suit, and Russell secured P1 with a 1m26.745s lap on the green-walled compound, ahead of an impressive looking Lawson and Hadjar. Newly-minted world champion Antonelli only just managed to advance in 10th, knocking out Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton , who is already due to start at the rear anyway with a power unit penalty. Oscar Piastri also failed to advance, the McLaren driver a disappointing 12th. Haas rookie Rafael Camara had done well to progress to Q2 despite going off, but he then crashed at the end of the session by going straight into the wall at turn 12, bringing out a late red flag. In the second Racing Bulls car, Arvid Lindblad was dumped out in 14th due to a power unit issue, followed by Carlos Sainz in the Williams . Red Bull's Max Verstappen , who joins Hamilton at the back of the grid with an engine penalty of his own, did not go out in Q2 and was classified 16th. Following an earlier downpour and more rain on the horizon, Q1 started on time but with conditions worsening right before the session went green. Several drivers immediately parked their cars to be pushed back and exchange their intermediates for full wet tyres. Those who did go out confirmed that was a good idea, with cars heading straight back in after reporting aquaplaning as race control red-flagged the session. top.title: Toto Wolff explains the emotional Mercedes factory email leaked online
top.description: Motorsport photo Securing a Formula 1 world championship triggers a lot of emotions, and, usually, a lot of champagne. But for Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff, Kimi Antonelli's historic title win in Mexico City triggered a sudden urge to write an incredibly long essay to his staff. During the Free Practice 3 broadcast at the Brazilian Grand Prix, Sky Sports F1 presenter Simon Lazenby brought up a rather inspiring internal Mercedes email that recently made its way onto the internet. Wolff, in classic deadpan fashion, immediately roasted the broadcaster for actually taking the time to read the whole thing. "Did you read such a long email? It was quite long," Wolff joked. When Lazenby confirmed he read it all the way through, Wolff fired back, "I was surprised the last time I wrote it [something that long] was under severe pressure in school." Deflecting the spotlight Jokes aside, Wolff explained the emotional catalyst behind the massive message. As the guy who officially signed off on putting a teenager into Lewis Hamilton's legendary seat, Wolff was getting flooded with congratulatory messages from the media and the paddock. He didn't want it. "So why was it spontaneous? Because I got so much praise on that Sunday night about giving him the opportunity and in Italy," Wolff explained to the Sky Sports crew. "And it's something that makes you very proud. But I felt I needed to give credit to all the people that maybe weren't so much in the spotlight." Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Formula 1 is the ultimate team sport, and pushing a rookie through a brutal 2025 slump to a 2026 World Championship took an entire village of engineers, strategists, and mentors. Wolff wanted to make sure the men and women turning the wrenches and crunching the data knew this was their trophy, too. "This email, he didn't even give it justice because there is many more that were part of the decision-making process and getting him to where he was," the Mercedes boss continued. "And that's why I felt like I need to at least express my gratitude to the big team." The LinkedIn leak So how did a private, internal factory memo end up public? You can thank Mercedes communications boss and senior leadership figure Bradley Lord for that. When Wolff hit send on his emotional late-night draft, Lord apparently decided the message was far too good to keep locked inside the company inbox. Bradley Lord, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal Bradley Lord, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal "And then Bradley felt that was a more clever email than normally," Wolff laughed. "So he put it on LinkedIn, and that it was when it was spread." It might have been an accidental public relations masterclass, but it offered fans a rare, unscripted look at the nurturing culture Wolff has built inside the Mercedes garage. top.title: Five Things Learned: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Manchester City (Premier League)
top.description: Five Things Learned: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Manchester City (Premier League) City slumped to a third straight Premier League loss with defeat away at Nottingham Forest to fall six points behind reigning champions and leaders Arsenal . Enzo Maresca's side headed into Saturday evening's game at the City Ground on a losing streak, having been defeated by both Aston Villa and Brighton and Hove Albion in recent weeks. Forest, who hadn't scored at home all season, took the lead early on through Jair Cunha, who effortlessly slotted past the out-of-form Gianluigi Donnarumma. After a tepid first-half, the visitors' attack sprang into life as Rayan Cherki smashed in Jeremy Doku's deflected cross to restore hope among the travelling fans. City failed to capitalise on this for the ten minutes following, and Delap instead notched a superb second, finishing off a deadly counter-attack for Forest. Here are five things we learned from Manchester City 's dismal display against Nottingham Forest : 1. Another early goal conceded For a third Premier League game in a row, City conceded from an early goal, putting them behind after just six minutes this time out. There are plenty of issues to highlight from the Nottingham Forest game as well as the past defeats, but the importance of conceding early itself cannot be understated. After taking the lead, the teams work harder and are far harder to break down, whilst the Blues themselves appear to be dejected each time a goal goes in. For previous sides, it would set the hackles up and Manchester City would hit back twice as hard, but this current group seem to struggle to rally back in times of adversity. This is all the more puzzling when you factor in the scenarios the team has already overcome this season, like being a man down at United or conceding three to Sunderland . I think we have all said it multiple times already this campaign, especially in recent weeks, but why on earth, and the wider solar system, is Ayyoub Bouaddi not playing? The Moroccan has looked excellent since joining in the summer, demonstrating the talent to dictate a midfield even at the young age of 19. Despite this, Enzo Maresca continues to select the trio of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki for the majority of games. Now there's no doubting the England international has been one of City's best players this season but he is far too exposed in that line-up without the likes of Bouaddi to help cover. This was predictably once again the case versus Nottingham Forest, who sliced through the midfield far too easily to net their goals. top.title: A Bears win on Sunday could catapult Caleb Williams back into the MVP race
top.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 2: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears reacts after the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on November 2, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before the 2026 season started, Caleb Williams was seen as a dark-horse MVP candidate. He was coming off an exciting first year with Ben Johnson, with a highlight reel a mile long. He was the Madden cover athlete, and as the offseason progressed, the buzz around Caleb and the Chicago Bears kept building. After they dropped a 50-burger in Week 1, the NFL shifted the hype train into high gear, and the Bears were the lead story on every NFL show. But then Week 2 and Brian Flores’ Minnesota Vikings defense came to town, and coupled with a steady downpour, Chicago’s offense never got on track. Then a fourth-quarter hamstring injury as the Bears were driving inside the Minnesota 1o yard line would sideline Williams for the next three games, seemingly ending his Most Valuable Player chances. The Bears went 2-1 in his absence, but since his return, Williams and the Bears haven’t trailed in any of their three games, and he’s completing 73.8% of his passes for 860 yards, 4 touchdowns, no turnovers, and a passer rating of 111.3. The last two weeks, he diced up the defenses of the last two Super Bowl teams, and his MVP odds have shot back up according to our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook . Right now, he’s at +800 to win MVP, trailing only the Buffalo Bills’ Josh Allen (+175), the Cincinnati Bengals’ Joe Burrow (+450), the San Fransocso 49ers’ Brock Purdy (+550 ), and the Jacksonville Jaguars’ Trevor Lawrence (+600). Earlier this week, we outlined how difficult it has been historically for a player to win the Most Valuable Player award after missing time during the season, but there is a precedent for him to do it, and another big game on Sunday Night Football could get him back in the conversation.

top.description: Louisville 107, Morehead State 57. The game, frankly, wasn’t that close. The Cards were ahead 46-33 at intermission. U of L registered points on their first 3 possessions after the break. With 17:49 to go, the Eagles’ first deuce after halftime cut the margin to 53-35. State’s next tally came with 6:48 to play. During that interim, Louisville netted 33 in a row. Such was the level of domination, that’s not even the most lopsided stat of the afternoon. U of L grabbed 59 rebounds against the height challenged visitors. That’s two more boards than the vanquished scored points. The 2011 NCAA Regional this was not. Even balanced — moving the orange against such a lesser foe wasn’t an issue — seven Cardinals tallied double digits. Led by Obi Ekezie’s 20, and Karter Knox’s 15. Will Hanke scored on a nifty up and under the first time he touched the rock. Obi snared 13 boards. Flory Bidunga grabbed 7. Four guys had six, including Isaac Ellis. A couple more had five. It was a team effort. Every guy on the floor contributed. Defense was played. * * * * * Moments/ Trends that stood out: Alvaro Folgueiras’s skip pass to Jackson Shelstad for a wide open triple on the first possession of the 2d half. Our resident Real Madrid fan, with whom the offense starts more often than not, led U of L with 6 assists. Three during the Cardinals’ 11-2 run that opened play after the break. Louisville ended up a “respectable” 20/28 at the charity stripe. That is also deceptive. It could prove to be this squad’s Achilles Heel. The guys who tend to get hacked the most are not the best at the line. Seth Trimble, not Chucky Hepburn at FT line. To be monitored. Another bad habit: Flory Bidunga slaps and reaches at the ball. Will foul trouble be an issue in a big game? Karter Knox has a scorer’s mentality. The team appears legitimately unselfish. 21 assists. Eight minutes into the game, U of L had turned it over already four times. But only coughed it up three more times the rest of the tilt. De’Shayne Montgomery’s stint on the IR does have one blessing. Isaac Ellis is getting more PT early than he might otherwise. Such that my peeps and I have been trading possible nicknames. Doc: The Pebble. Gets in your shoe and bugs the shit out of you. Smarts: Mayhem. Ellis is clear team leader in floor burns. A fun afternoon, a walkover, one filled with positive signs. — c d kaplan

nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, have defeated Japan 2-1 to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The Flamingos secured the historic victory on Saturday at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat, to claim their first title in the competition. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring for Nigeria in the 39th minute with a long-range effort that slipped through the hands of the Japanese goalkeeper. Nigeria doubled their advantage shortly after the restart, with Oluebube Umejiaku finding the net in the 47th minute to put the Flamingos in control. Japan fought back and reduced the deficit through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute. The Japanese side pushed for an equaliser, but Nigeria held on to secure the 2-1 victory. nigeria.title: Arsenal Edge Hull To Extend Premier League Lead As Tottenham Lose To Leeds
nigeria.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted by Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 league games. Arsenal, who bossed possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that the German forward was in an offside position in the build-up. (Photo by Henry Nicholls / AFP) Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled and Odegaard fired home from close range. Arsenal manager Arteta said he was happy with the performance but wanted his team to be more clinical after they recorded a third 1-0 win in four league games. “I think it is time to praise my players. What they have done not only today but after the international break is remarkable because of the games,” he told the BBC. He added: “We have some great moments, we need to put the chances we are creating against the opponent into the scoreline. nigeria.description: Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham said Saturday he hoped to fulfil a “huge dream” by playing alongside brother Jude after being called up to the England squad. On Friday, England manager Thomas Tuchel named Jobe, 21, in England’s 25-man squad for November’s Nations League fixtures with Croatia and Spain. Speaking after Dortmund’s 2-1 home win over Elversberg in the Bundesliga, Jobe said he and brother had acted out playing together for England when they were kids. “It’s really good. I don’t want to get too carried away, but it’s obviously a big dream for me and for Jude as well,” the younger Bellingham told DAZN. “Since we were young, we reenacted that so many times in the garden or wherever, in the park, playing for England together. “So it’s a huge dream. It’s not happened yet, so I don’t want to jinx or say it too early, but yeah, I’m really excited.” Jobe has captained England’s under-21s but this is his first senior call-up. Real Madrid midfielder Jude, 23, who also made his England debut while playing for Dortmund, now has 60 England caps. nigeria.title: ‘Collect Their Money, Spend It, But Vote Your Heart’, Makinde Tells Supporters
nigeria.description: The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, has urged his supporters to accept money offered by politicians but vote according to their conscience. Makinde gave the advice on Saturday at his presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State, where he told supporters not to feel guilty about collecting such money while remaining loyal to their preferred candidate. “Don’t bother at all. When they bring money, it is your money, collect it, but vote your heart and I know your heart is with us and APM,” he said. ﻿ The Oyo governor pledged to reset Nigeria’s economy, security architecture and socio-political environment if elected president. He said Nigerians unhappy with the state of the country should support his “Reset Nigeria” agenda. “If you are not happy with the way things are in our country today, if you are not happy that there is no enough inclusivity, if you are not happy that your government cannot tell you the truth, they cannot handle our issues with sincerity, then there is only one part for us and the part is to reset Nigeria. So, I am asking you today to be a resetter,” Makinde said. Also addressing the rally, the party’s vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, said the politics of lies, deceit and hypocrisy was threatening democracy in Nigeria. He said the APM’s reset agenda was designed to tackle these challenges and ensure that anyone elected into government would be committed to honesty and sincerity. nigeria.title: Rivers crisis: You’ll not regret choosing peace, Tinubu assures Fubara
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has assured Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, that he would not regret his decision to embrace peace and respect the intervention of political elders in resolving the crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu gave the assurance on Saturday while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt. He said, “To me, I intervened on your behalf. Similarly, to Fubara, Your Excellency, the host governor of today, I want to thank you specifically for maturity, understanding, respect for the wisdom of elders. “When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat, Fubara. You will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive,” Tinubu said. The political crisis, which erupted in October 2023, followed a breakdown in relations between Fubara and his predecessor, now Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, over control of the state’s political structure. The crisis escalated in March 2025 when Tinubu declared a state of emergency in the state , suspending Fubara, his deputy, Ngozi Odu, and members of the House of Assembly for six months. Fubara returned to office in September 2025 following the expiration of the emergency rule. However, political tensions resurfaced, with lawmakers initiating another impeachment process against him and his deputy in January 2026. Efforts to reconcile the feuding camps gained momentum in June 2025 when Tinubu convened a meeting involving Fubara, Wike and members of the Rivers State House of Assembly at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. nigeria.title: Arsenal edge past Hull to stretch Premier League lead
nigeria.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted at Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 games. Manchester City can close the gap to three points if they beat struggling Nottingham Forest in the late kick-off as they seek to avoid a third straight defeat. Arsenal, who hogged possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled, with Odegaard firing home from close range. – VAR controversy – In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run. The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared. Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.” Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: Toto Wolff explains the emotional Mercedes factory email leaked online
sports.description: Motorsport photo Securing a Formula 1 world championship triggers a lot of emotions, and, usually, a lot of champagne. But for Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff, Kimi Antonelli's historic title win in Mexico City triggered a sudden urge to write an incredibly long essay to his staff. During the Free Practice 3 broadcast at the Brazilian Grand Prix, Sky Sports F1 presenter Simon Lazenby brought up a rather inspiring internal Mercedes email that recently made its way onto the internet. Wolff, in classic deadpan fashion, immediately roasted the broadcaster for actually taking the time to read the whole thing. "Did you read such a long email? It was quite long," Wolff joked. When Lazenby confirmed he read it all the way through, Wolff fired back, "I was surprised the last time I wrote it [something that long] was under severe pressure in school." Deflecting the spotlight Jokes aside, Wolff explained the emotional catalyst behind the massive message. As the guy who officially signed off on putting a teenager into Lewis Hamilton's legendary seat, Wolff was getting flooded with congratulatory messages from the media and the paddock. He didn't want it. "So why was it spontaneous? Because I got so much praise on that Sunday night about giving him the opportunity and in Italy," Wolff explained to the Sky Sports crew. "And it's something that makes you very proud. But I felt I needed to give credit to all the people that maybe weren't so much in the spotlight." Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Formula 1 is the ultimate team sport, and pushing a rookie through a brutal 2025 slump to a 2026 World Championship took an entire village of engineers, strategists, and mentors. Wolff wanted to make sure the men and women turning the wrenches and crunching the data knew this was their trophy, too. "This email, he didn't even give it justice because there is many more that were part of the decision-making process and getting him to where he was," the Mercedes boss continued. "And that's why I felt like I need to at least express my gratitude to the big team." The LinkedIn leak So how did a private, internal factory memo end up public? You can thank Mercedes communications boss and senior leadership figure Bradley Lord for that. When Wolff hit send on his emotional late-night draft, Lord apparently decided the message was far too good to keep locked inside the company inbox. Bradley Lord, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal Bradley Lord, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal "And then Bradley felt that was a more clever email than normally," Wolff laughed. "So he put it on LinkedIn, and that it was when it was spread." It might have been an accidental public relations masterclass, but it offered fans a rare, unscripted look at the nurturing culture Wolff has built inside the Mercedes garage. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before. Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. Read more Extreme heat is now making cities unlivable. How can we survive it? In the UK in 2022, temperatures exceeded 40°C (104 ° F) for the first time in history, despite predictions that such a milestone was probably still years away. Likewise, the 2021 heatwave in the Pacific Northwest saw temperatures hit extremes that far outstripped climate model projections. One team thinks the answer lies partly in the soil. Scientists already knew that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface, heating up the land. science.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
science.description: null The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened. We'd both seen photographs of M31 — a vast spiral galaxy with a brilliant center, sweeping dust lanes and hundreds of billions of stars. What we were actually looking at was a grayish blur that could easily have been mistaken for a mark on the eyepiece. That apparent disappointment is now my favorite part of finding Andromeda because the unimpressive smudge is real. The light entering your eyes has been traveling across space for about 2.5 million years. No screen, photograph or telescope is necessary. You are intercepting ancient light in your backyard. Technically, the Triangulum Galaxy (M33), about 2.7 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye, so it is therefore the most distant object the naked eye can see. But not mine — I've never seen it. M31 is a much more realistic naked-eye target. What's happening and when to look The Andromeda galaxy is at its most dramatic in photographs, not an eyepiece. (Image credit: Created using Canva and a base image from Starry Night) Early November is an excellent time to find M31 from the Northern Hemisphere. It's high and well placed during the evening, and this week the moon is becoming particularly cooperative. New Moon falls around Nov. 9, giving us several evenings with little or no moonlight to wash out faint deep-sky objects. I usually begin with the star Alpheratz, one of the corner stars of the Great Square of Pegasus. You go two stars left, two stars up, and you arrive at M31. Another route — and a good way to check you're in the right place — starts in Cassiopeia, the distinctive W-shaped constellation high in the northeastern sky on autumn evenings. You can use its second V-shape as an arrow pointing straight at M31. You can do that star-hop with the naked eye or a pair of binoculars, but M31 is visible to the naked eye only under a very dark sky. However, don't look for a miniature version of the photographs. Expect a faint, elongated patch with a slightly brighter middle. There's another beginner trap to avoid. science.description: null Sometimes science can seem really counter-intuitive. For example, occasionally in astronomy, you can see more with less light. Case in point: the emergence of a giant planet in observations made by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), when astronomers found a way to block out light from the planet's parent star. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , in question is 51 Eridani b (51 ERI b), a gas giant with the same mass as around 11 Jupiters that orbits a star located around 97 light-years away. 51 ERI b was discovered back in 2015 by ground-based telescopes, but the planet was missing from observations of the system made by the JWST. That wasn't a failing of the JWST itself; no one is doubting the observing capabilities of the most powerful telescope humanity has ever hoisted into orbit around Earth. Instead, it was a result of starlight from the star 51 ERI A obscuring this intimidatingly massive world. The brightest planets are 100,000 times fainter than their host stars, meaning spotting them is like observing a firefly hovering around a lighthouse. Even using a tool called a coronagraph to block the star isn't enough to reveal the planet, as that doesn't stop all the starlight. The only solution to this glaring problem is a computer program to wipe out the starlight. "For the past 20 years, astronomers have tackled this problem by observing a different star and using its image as a reference," Jason Wang of Northwestern University explained in a statement . "Then, they subtract that reference image from the original observation to remove the unwanted glare to reveal faint planets that otherwise might be hidden." There is a problem with this process, however. Even the most stable telescopes "wobble." For instance, the JWST requires cryocoolers to keep its NIRCam instrument super cold, and those coolers have little motors that can cause the mirrors to vibrate. This movement, however slight, causes a scatter in starlight. The result is enough glare remaining to obscure a planet, but Wang and colleagues developed a new approach to this problem. Telescopes their more stable digital twins The new approach taken by the team is dubbed Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP), and it involves creating a digital "twin" of a telescope. Essentially a virtual replica that simulates how starlight travels through the telescope's mirrors and reaches its detectors. This twin is then fine-tuned to account for millions of tiny imperfections in the original telescope. The digital twin is then tweaked until it aligns with observations from the actual telescope. Astronomers can then remove the simulated glare from the original image. To assess the validity of the technique, the researchers took a second look at JWST observations of two star systems with known exoplanets, HIP 65426 and 51 Eridani , and one system, TYC 5899, with no known planets. science.title: M30’s Sparkling Stars
science.description: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini This NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image released Nov. 5, 2026, provides a lesson in galactic history. The sparkling collection of stars is named Messier 30 (M30) after the French astronomer, Charles Messier , who cataloged M30 and other diffuse objects that might be mistaken for comets in the early telescopes of Messier’s time. M30 lies about 27,500 light-years away in the constellation Capricornus. Read more about this group of stars and what scientists can learn from it. Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G.
